desks.Dividends: Apple goes ex-dividend today, Thu Nov 12, at $0.27 per quarter, unchanged, payable Nov 16. Microsoft goes ex-dividend Thu Nov 19 at $0.98, the first payment at the raised rate (+7.7%) and its 24th consecutive annual increase, payable Dec 10. Nvidia has not yet declared its fourth-quarter dividend; a December ex-date is plausible from cadence but UNVERIFIED. SPY and QQQ December ex-dates are unconfirmed. Tesla pays no dividend.
desks.Earnings: Nvidia is the only watchlist name reporting in the window, Tue Nov 17 after close, with consensus of about $109.2 billion in revenue and EPS of about $2.47 (Schwab, Nov 4) against company guidance of $108.0 billion, plus or minus 2%. Options imply a move of 10.4-10.8%, above the 7.8% 10-year average earnings-day move, and the Q4 guide is likely to matter more than the Q3 print. Premium into a binary event is to be avoided. Apple, Microsoft and Tesla reported in the last three weeks; their next prints are estimated for late January 2027 (UNVERIFIED, unconfirmed).
desks.Futures: The EIA weekly petroleum report, released Thu Nov 12 after a Veterans Day delay, showed commercial crude up 4.657 million barrels to 414.4 million, against a draw expected, ending five straight weekly draws; gasoline rose 1.799 million and distillate 4.071 million, though distillate remains 8% below its 5-year average. WTI still rose 2.27% to $88.49 in the US session after the US said it is no longer interested in a deal with Iran, so futures are pricing Strait-constraint risk, not the inventory surplus. The November WASDE landed Tue Nov 10: corn yield cut to 179.6 bushels per acre, December corn up 9 3/4 cents and January soybeans up 39 3/4 cents on the day. OPEC's November report left demand forecasts unchanged. Abu Dhabi talks ended with no ceasefire.
desks.Parity: No new SPY or QQQ parity-violation report or index-methodology change was published in the last 24 hours. Put-call parity on SPX held within about 0.06 index points in the Nov 4-5 checks, and an independent analysis of 2,565 CBOE SPX quotes found parity essentially exact. The standing S&P style-methodology change takes effect before the open on Dec 21, with pro-forma files Dec 4; it changes growth/value classification, not S&P 500 membership, so there is no direct SPY composition change. FTSE Russell's style consultation remains open, comments due Dec 11. The S&P MegaCap consultation concluded with no changes.
desks.Premium: All six verdicts are WINDOW-CONTINGENT. The Nov 5 jump still drives 41-55% of each 20-day realized-variance window, so the gap between implied vol and trailing realized vol on five of six names at 8 days to expiry is most plausibly the jump inflating realized, not cheap premium. Nvidia is the standout: at-the-money implied vol of 88-92% on both the Nov 13 and Nov 20 expiries, about 1.7 times its 20-day realized vol of 51.9%, with a flat-to-inverted term structure, so the elevation is not purely earnings-driven. SPY and QQQ closing marks fail put-call parity (+$0.86 and +$1.45), so those implied-vol levels are indicative, not precise. IV rank is UNVERIFIED for all six names: no free IV-history source is available.
desks.Quant lab: Seven new candidates were scored and added to the ledger (#261-267), all WATCH, with no TEST or INTEGRATE movement. The top score, #261 (59), is an arbitrage-free neural operator for European call-price surfaces; its key doctrine point, source-reported and UNVERIFIED, is that a nearest arbitrage-free correction of an unconstrained surface need not exist, so post-processing cannot restore no-arbitrage. #267 is EODHD's Options Explorer; the chain is a paid add-on, so the free value is the code pattern, not data. The Nov 11 submission window is provisional, not confirmed empty, and must be re-covered next run.

items.detail: FRED as of Nov 10-11: the effective federal funds rate is 3.88%, the 2-year Treasury 4.73%, and the 10-year 4.98%, putting the 2s10s slope at +25 basis points, down from +35 on Nov 6. The 2-year rose 17 basis points in a day against 10 at the long end, so the market is repricing near-term policy expectations upward. SOFR minus the effective funds rate is +1 basis point — no funding stress. Front-end repricing with long rates near 5% is discount-rate pressure on growth multiples, most on the watchlist's long-duration names.
items.title: Rates: the curve flattened 10 bp in two sessions, with the long end near 5%
